source.title: Convex Dominance in Deep Learning I: A Scaling Law of Loss and Learning Rate
source.authors: Zhi-Qi Bu; Shi-Yun Xu; J. Mao

record.file_problem: Text appears to contain the full paper. Some figure labels and equations are garbled in the web extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests loss prediction and scaling with a different formulation: loss versus training horizon under a learning-rate schedule, rather than the original parameter/token/compute scaling-law fits.
record.gate_note: The study also reports sequence-to-sequence loss predictions from learning-rate schedules for ResNet18 and GPT2. These predict later iterations within a run, not larger runs from smaller runs, so they are not included as rows for the listed versions. It refits loss-versus-learning-rate data from Li et al. and reconstructed Chinchilla data; cited results are not treated as independent experiments. It does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or downstream-task performance.
record.test_reason: The study fits held-out (test/validation) LM loss against training horizon with the form L = L∞ + Q/sqrt(T), under learning rates rescaled per horizon. It does this in its own GPT2 pretraining runs (0.1B to 7B) and in a refit of the reconstructed Chinchilla runs. It also tests the form in fine-tuning and VLM settings. This is a different method aimed at loss scaling in tokens, so T2. The exponent is fixed at 0.5 by theory, not fitted.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that deep learning behaves convex-like after early training and that loss is predictable from the learning-rate schedule. Under 1/sqrt(T)-scaled learning rates with qualified schedules, loss converges as O(1/sqrt(T)). They build a law extrapolating about 80x in horizon and about 70x in model size. Correction: the model-size extrapolation is transfer of the optimal learning rate from 0.1B, with loss laws fitted per size. They note test-loss prediction fails under severe overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a learning-rate/loss scaling formulation based on convex-style bounds and data-driven fitting. It is not a reproduction of the original parameter/token/compute scaling-law method or compute-optimal allocation experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported fitted coefficients vary with optimizer, model size, batch size, weight decay, clipping, momentum, and random seed. Test-loss prediction fails in the severe-overfitting setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal peak learning rate scales as eta_ref*/sqrt(T): eta_ref*=10 for Muon-NSGD and 0.3 for AdamW. It transfers from 0.1B to 1B/7B. Loss vs peak LR in Li et al. data fits L∞+q1²/(Tη)+ηq2² with R2≥0.95.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under horizon-aware decaying schedules, the optimal peak learning rate scales as T^-0.5 and transfers across model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-run sequence-to-sequence loss prediction from the learning-rate schedule: R2≥0.95 for ResNet18 and GPT2 across SGD/AdamW/Muon and four schedules (Figs 2–5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss trajectories within a run are predictable from the learning-rate sequence via a convex-style bound.

record.problems: The Chinchilla losses are reconstructed from another study, and the text does not identify their loss split. The Chinchilla batch size is not released in the cited work and is assumed constant. Many results are reported in figures without individual numerical values. The authors report a failure to predict test loss under severe overfitting.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the reported Table 6 fits or the V2, V5, and V7 results included here. Sequence-to-sequence predictions from Figures 2–5 are not included because they predict later iterations within the same run rather than any listed version.

untested.parts: Scaling in parameter count and in compute; the exponent (fixed at 0.5 by construction, not estimated).
Predicting larger models' loss from smaller models. Only the learning rate is transferred across sizes; each size's loss law is fit on its own runs.
Entirely untested. Figure 6 MoE shapes come from Li et al. and concern learning-rate curves.
Video, large-scale image pretraining, and transfer performance.
Comparisons of published exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices.

missing.what: ViT (Tiny/Small/Base) and ResNet (18/34/50) on ImageNet within 1 epoch: 1/sqrt(T) holds for both train and test loss, with slightly different coefficients.
2B Chinchilla model fit R2=0.9986, with all losses within 1% relative error. Fitted L∞ decreases log-linearly with model size and 2q1q2 roughly increases.

Ablation (GPT2 0.1B, Muon): batch size 64 vs 512 changes Q from 23.9 to 39.5 and L∞ from 2.830 to 2.967. Seed, clipping, momentum and weight decay change coefficients slightly; R2 is 0.995–1.000 throughout.
missing.versions: V7 (coefficient-level setup dependence only; exponent fixed)

record.verdict_notes: The Chinchilla rows are a refit of original-source data (Hoffmann via Besiroglu), not independent experiments. Weigh them accordingly, especially sizes with only 3 horizons. The 1/sqrt(T) form uses per-horizon LR rescaling and a fixed exponent of 0.5, so it cannot estimate the token exponent, and differs from Chinchilla's fitted data exponent. The GPT2 runs repeat OpenWebText for up to ~30 epochs; the authors say test loss stays close to train loss. Fits hold only past an early-training threshold (T>2.5k for GPT2, T>2000 for the VLM).

versions.untested_parts: The analyzed Chinchilla data tests loss against training horizon/tokens at fixed model sizes. The study does not test power-law scaling in parameter count or compute independently, nor establish that the other quantities are not bottlenecks. The text does not state whether the reconstructed Chinchilla losses are held-out losses.

Tests the study's own loss-and-learning-rate scaling formulation, including horizon extrapolation and transfer across model sizes; it does not test all original scaling-law fits or their full range of training setups.
No sweep over fixed-compute parameter/token allocations or measurement of a compute-optimal split.
No controlled comparison establishing how depth, width, or other architecture details affect loss at fixed parameter count.
Tests fine-tuning and one vision-language fine-tuning setting. Does not test image/video pretraining, repeated-data pretraining as a separate regime, or transfer performance.

The study shows a loss-fit failure in an overfitting setting and reports setup-dependent fitted coefficients in an ablation. It does not directly compare published parameter/token/compute exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting methods.
